title: Astronomers Just Found the First Green Star. It's Eating Its Planets

scenes.text: Astronomers just found the first green star. It's eating its planets.
326 light-years away sits a dead star. A white dwarf.
Normally a star can't be green. Its colour comes from heat alone: red, orange, white, blue.
But this one has been swallowing rocky rubble from its own planets. Rubble full of sodium.
The sodium soaks up the red and orange light. What's left, to a human eye, is green.
One day our Sun dies too. If it eats its planets, it might go green.

description:
In October 2026, astronomers at the University of Warwick reported the first known green star: a cool white dwarf called WD J1330+6435, about 326 light-years away.
A star's colour normally depends only on its temperature, but this dead star has been pulling in rocky debris from its own planetary system. The sodium in that debris absorbs the red and orange light, and models of human colour vision show that what remains would look green.
What colour do you think our Sun will end up? Comment below.
first_comment: The same team also found the reddest star ever recorded, a salmon-pink white dwarf 48 light-years away, coloured by carbon rising from its core. Green or pink: which would you rather see in the sky?
